claim: The age and sex of studied animals profoundly impact experimental outcomes in biomedical research.
source: The age and sex of studied animals profoundly impact experimental outcomes in biomedical research.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Most preclinical studies in mice use a wide-spanning age range from 4 to 20 weeks.
source: However, most preclinical studies in mice use a wide-spanning age range from 4 to 20 weeks and do not assess male and female mice in parallel.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction (Flórez-Vargas et al., 2016).

claim: Most preclinical studies do not assess male and female mice in parallel.
source: However, most preclinical studies in mice use a wide-spanning age range from 4 to 20 weeks and do not assess male and female mice in parallel.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The study uncovered significant differences when comparing male and female mice at adolescent (4 weeks) and adult (14 weeks) age.
source: Remarkably, we uncovered significant differences when comparing male and female mice at adolescent (4 weeks) and adult (14 weeks) age.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The study deciphered protein subsets and networks that were correlated with the age and/or sex of mice.
source: Our analysis deciphered protein subsets and networks that were correlated with the age and/or sex of mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the proteomics data and network analysis presented in the results.

claim: Proteins/biological pathways with known (patho)physiological relevance include homeostasis and epidermal signaling in skin.
source: Notably, among these were proteins/biological pathways with known (patho)physiological relevance, e.g., homeostasis and epidermal signaling in skin, and, in SCN, multiple myelin proteins and regulators of neuronal development.
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis and comparison with known biological functions.

claim: Multiple myelin proteins and regulators of neuronal development in SCN showed age and/or sex differences.
source: Notably, among these were proteins/biological pathways with known (patho)physiological relevance, e.g., homeostasis and epidermal signaling in skin, and, in SCN, multiple myelin proteins and regulators of neuronal development.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data showing differential expression of myelin proteins.

claim: Various proteins associated with distinct skin diseases exhibited significant abundance changes in dependence on age and/or sex.
source: Extensive comparisons with available databases revealed that various proteins associated with distinct skin diseases and pain exhibited significant abundance changes in dependence on age and/or sex.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the proteomics data with skin disease databases.

claim: Various proteins associated with pain exhibited significant abundance changes in dependence on age and/or sex.
source: Extensive comparisons with available databases revealed that various proteins associated with distinct skin diseases and pain exhibited significant abundance changes in dependence on age and/or sex.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the proteomics data with pain gene databases.

claim: The Jackson Laboratory considers the mouse strain C57BL/6J of mature adult physiology only at 12 weeks of age.
source: Therefore, the Jackson Laboratory (https://www.jax.org) considers the widely used mouse strain C57BL/6J of mature adult physiology only at 12 weeks of age (Flurkey et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Flurkey et al., 2007.

claim: In mice, the first 12 weeks of life are characterized by pronounced changes in terms of growth and development of all organs and systems.
source: In mice, the first 12 weeks of life are characterized by pronounced changes in terms of growth and development of all organs and systems.
evidence: This is supported by citations to established knowledge about mouse development.

claim: Most preclinical studies still do not perform experiments on male and female rodents in parallel.
source: Despite recently enforced policies by funding agencies to include animals of both sexes, most preclinical studies still do not perform experiments on male and female rodents in parallel, exhibit gaps in data analysis by sex, and often pool animals of both sexes and a wide range of ages (between 4 and 20 weeks) (Flórez-Vargas et al., 2016) given time and financial constraints (Garcia-Sifuentes and Maney, 2021; Woitowich et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature on sex as a biological variable.

claim: Most preclinical studies often pool animals of both sexes and a wide range of ages (between 4 and 20 weeks).
source: Despite recently enforced policies by funding agencies to include animals of both sexes, most preclinical studies still do not perform experiments on male and female rodents in parallel, exhibit gaps in data analysis by sex, and often pool animals of both sexes and a wide range of ages (between 4 and 20 weeks) (Flórez-Vargas et al., 2016) given time and financial constraints (Garcia-Sifuentes and Maney, 2021; Woitowich et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on experimental design practices.

claim: These practices may negatively impact reproducibility across studies.
source: These practices may negatively impact reproducibility across studies, increase data variability, conceal differences or generate artifactual results, and, consequently, hamper translationally oriented preclinical research (Flórez-Vargas et al., 2016; Jackson et al., 2017; Oliva et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on reproducibility in preclinical research.

claim: Mouse behavior experiments assessing paw sensitivity have routinely been performed in mice aged between 6 and 20 weeks.
source: Mouse behavior experiments assessing paw sensitivity have routinely been performed in mice aged between 6 and 20 weeks (Hanack et al., 2015; Moehring et al., 2018; Zheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific studies on mouse behavior.

claim: Studies in cultured peripheral sensory neurons or keratinocytes have used mice aged 4–6 weeks.
source: Studies in cultured peripheral sensory neurons or keratinocytes have used mice aged 4–6 weeks (Hanack et al., 2015; Poole et al., 2014), 4–8 weeks (Zheng et al., 2019), 7–10 weeks (Narayanan et al., 2018; Narayanan et al., 2016), or 8–16 weeks (Sadler et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific studies on cultured neurons and keratinocytes.

claim: 4-week-old adolescent mice were more sensitive to innocuous tactile stimulation than 12-week-old adult mice.
source: In particular, 4-week-old adolescent mice were more sensitive to innocuous tactile stimulation than 12-week-old adult mice.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Michel et al., 2020.

claim: Age-dependent changes in tactile sensitivity correlated with similar changes in the activity of the mechanically activated ion channel Piezo2.
source: Interestingly, these observations correlated with similar changes in the activity of the mechanically activated ion channel Piezo2 and age-dependent transcriptome changes in peripheral sensory neurons.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Michel et al., 2020.

claim: Transcript levels only show limited correspondence with protein levels.
source: This is highly relevant as transcript levels only show limited correspondence with protein levels, which renders the functional interpretation of transcriptome results difficult, in particular under dynamic conditions such as development, maturation, and disease (Liu et al., 2016; Schwanhäusser et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies comparing transcriptome and proteome data.

claim: Deep proteome profiling of complex tissues is still challenging, above all, for low abundant and transmembrane proteins.
source: However, in contrast to well-established RNA-seq approaches, deep proteome profiling of complex tissues is still challenging, above all, for low abundant and transmembrane proteins.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about technical challenges in proteomics.

claim: DIA-PASEF has been shown to offer superior performance for deep profiling compared to DDA-PASEF.
source: The latter has been shown to offer superior performance for deep profiling (Meier et al., 2020), yet it has, thus far, only been applied by specialized laboratories given its high demands regarding technology and data analysis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Meier et al., 2020.

claim: The average correlations of quality controls were 0.98 and 0.99 for pooled skin and SCN samples, respectively.
source: The average correlations of quality controls were 0.98 and 0.99 for pooled skin and SCN samples, respectively, indicating highly consistent stability of the instrument setup.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: DIA-PASEF detected additional 4135 and 3926 protein groups in skin and SCN, respectively, compared to DDA-PASEF.
source: As shown in Figure 1C and D, protein identifications from DDA-PASEF were highly covered by DIA-PASEF experiments, and DIA-PASEF detected additional 4135 and 3926 protein groups in skin and SCN, respectively (Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Smaller coefficients of variation (CVs) were observed across all DIA-PASEF runs compared to DDA-PASEF.
source: Notably, we observed smaller coefficients of variation (CVs) across all DIA-PASEF runs (Figure 1E and F), indicating higher reproducibility compared to DDA-PASEF.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: More than 8600 protein IDs were quantified across experimental groups in paw skin.
source: In paw skin, we quantified > 8600 protein IDs across experimental groups (Figure 2A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The skin proteome covered approximately 70% of the most comprehensive human skin proteome dataset published so far.
source: Comparing this proteome dataset with the most comprehensive (human) skin proteome dataset (Dyring-Andersen et al., 2020) published so far, our skin proteome covered approximately 70% (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: All 50 known keratins and 19 collagens were identified in the skin proteome.
source: Nonetheless, we identified all 50 known keratins and 19 collagens.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: 13 members of the interleukin (IL) family and 11 of the S100 family were quantified in skin.
source: In addition to structural proteins, we also quantified 13 members of the interleukin (IL) family and 11 of the S100 family (Figure 2E), known to play essential roles in the context of inflammation and infection (Kozlyuk et al., 2019; Velazquez-Salinas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Approximately 8400 protein IDs were quantified across experimental groups in SCN.
source: In SCN, approx. 8400 protein IDs were quantified across experimental groups (Figure 2C, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The myelin proteome was nearly completely covered (94%; 1014/1077 described myelin proteins) in the SCN data.
source: Remarkably, the myelin proteome was nearly completely covered in our SCN data (94%); 1014/1077 described myelin proteins (Siems et al., 2020; Figure 2D), without a priori myelin enrichment as required in previous studies (Siems et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published myelin proteome data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Multiple ion channels were robustly quantified across SCN samples, including Trpv1 and several voltage-gated sodium channels.
source: Another indication as to the depth and high performance of our workflow is the fact that we robustly quantified multiple ion channels across SCN samples (Figure 2F, Figure 1—source data 2), such as Trpv1 and several voltage-gated sodium channels (e.g., Scn8a, Scn9a, Scn11a) – again without requiring preanalytical membrane preparations.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Age groups were clearly segregated by the first and second components in skin and SCN samples in PCA.
source: Age groups were clearly segregated by the first and second components in skin and SCN samples, indicating that age is a prominent discriminator in our study and associated differences can be tackled by whole-proteome analysis.
evidence: This is supported by the PCA plots shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: 234 and 94 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were found in female and male skin datasets, respectively, in age-dependent comparisons.
source: To explore this age dependency further, we applied a fold change (FC) cut-off (absolute log2 FC ≥ 0.585, i.e., an absolute FC of 1.5) in addition to a significance cut-off (q-value ≤ 0.05) and found 234 and 94 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in female and male skin datasets, respectively (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis of the proteomics data.

claim: 46 DEPs were shared between sexes in age-dependent comparisons of skin, while 188 and 48 DEPs were unique for female and male skin.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, 46 DEPs were shared between sexes, while 188 and 48 DEPs were unique for female and male skin (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the Venn diagram shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Skin development-related pathways such as 'protein hydroxylation' and 'collagen fibril organization' were enriched in 4-week skin compared to 14 weeks.
source: As expected, skin development-related pathways such as 'protein hydroxylation' and 'collagen fibril organization' were enriched in 4-week skin compared to 14 weeks.
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis of the proteomics data.

claim: Several proline/serine hydroxylases (e.g., P4ha2, P3h1, P4ha1) were highly expressed in 4-week skin together with members of collagens.
source: Specifically, several proline/serine hydroxylases (e.g., P4ha2, P3h1, P4ha1) were highly expressed in 4-week skin together with members of collagens (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In male skin, pathways of 'notch signaling' and 'extrinsic apoptotic signaling' were significantly enriched at 4 weeks.
source: In male skin, pathways of 'notch signaling' and 'extrinsic apoptotic signaling' were significantly enriched at 4 weeks, while 'actin-mediated cell contraction' and 'cellular component assembly involved in morphogenesis' were enriched at 14 weeks (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In male skin, 'actin-mediated cell contraction' and 'cellular component assembly involved in morphogenesis' were enriched at 14 weeks.
source: In male skin, pathways of 'notch signaling' and 'extrinsic apoptotic signaling' were significantly enriched at 4 weeks, while 'actin-mediated cell contraction' and 'cellular component assembly involved in morphogenesis' were enriched at 14 weeks (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In female skin, proteins annotated to multiple interconnected pathways were significantly enriched at 14 weeks compared to 4 weeks.
source: In female skin, proteins annotated to multiple interconnected pathways were significantly enriched at 14 weeks compared to 4 weeks (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 144 ligands and receptors of DRG were present in the skin dataset.
source: In total, 144 ligands and receptors of DRG were present in our skin dataset (Figure 3—source data 1), of which 12 were significantly regulated (q-value ≤ 0.05) when comparing 4-week to 14-week mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published ligand-receptor interaction data.

claim: 12 ligands and receptors of DRG were significantly regulated when comparing 4-week to 14-week mice in skin.
source: In total, 144 ligands and receptors of DRG were present in our skin dataset (Figure 3—source data 1), of which 12 were significantly regulated (q-value ≤ 0.05) when comparing 4-week to 14-week mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The ligand Lamb1 was found to be more abundant in 4-week female skin.
source: For example, the ligand Lamb1 was found to be more abundant in 4-week female skin.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: Lamb1 was reported to serve as an anchor point for end feet of radial glial cells and as a physical barrier to migrating neurons.
source: Lamb1 was reported to serve as an anchor point for end feet of radial glial cells and as a physical barrier to migrating neurons (Radmanesh et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Radmanesh et al., 2013.

claim: Mrc2 showed age-dependent statistical significance with higher expression at 4 weeks.
source: Interestingly, Mrc2 showed age-dependent statistical significance with higher expression at 4 weeks of age.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: 929 DEPs and 1269 DEPs were found in age-dependent comparisons of female and male SCN.
source: Differential expression analysis uncovered 929 DEPs and 1269 DEPs in age-dependent comparisons of female and male SCN (Figure 4A, Figure 1—source data 2), accounting for almost one-fifth of the here quantified SCN proteome.
evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 'Vesicle localization' had a higher z-score in 4-week SCN of both sexes.
source: For example, among common DEPs, 'vesicle localization' had a higher z-score in 4-week SCN of both sexes, while pathways related to 'neuron survival', 'neurotransmitter transport', and 'anterograde axonal transport' were more pronounced in 14-week SCN of both sexes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pathways related to 'neuron survival', 'neurotransmitter transport', and 'anterograde axonal transport' were more pronounced in 14-week SCN of both sexes.
source: For example, among common DEPs, 'vesicle localization' had a higher z-score in 4-week SCN of both sexes, while pathways related to 'neuron survival', 'neurotransmitter transport', and 'anterograde axonal transport' were more pronounced in 14-week SCN of both sexes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Superoxide dismutase (Sod1) was found to be less expressed in 4-week mice.
source: For instance, superoxide dismutase (Sod1) was found to be less expressed in 4-week mice and represents a connecting hub of two pathways related to nervous system function (Figure 4B) in line with its implication in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) (Pansarasa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: 144 DEPs from age-dependent comparisons were associated with the 'synapse' as revealed by querying SynGO.
source: Remarkably, 144 DEPs from age-dependent comparisons were associated with the 'synapse' as revealed by querying SynGO, a public reference for synapse research (Koopmans et al., 2019; Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with the SynGO database.

claim: Among the 56 immune cell ligands of neuronal receptors quantified in the SCN proteome, 19 showed age-dependent abundance changes in both sexes.
source: Among the 56 immune cell ligands of neuronal receptors quantified in the SCN proteome, 19 showed age-dependent abundance changes in both sexes such as Agrin (Agrn), Thy-1 membrane glycoprotein (Thy1), and several collagens (Figure 4C, Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 85 glial cell ligands of neuron receptors and 70 neuron ligands of glial cell receptors were found in the SCN proteome.
source: We found 85 glial cell ligands of neuron receptors and 70 neuron ligands of glial cell receptors in our SCN proteome, and, more interestingly, about one-third of ligand-receptor pairs showed strong age dependency (Figure 4—source data 3 and 4), e.g., limbic system-associated membrane protein (Lsamp), a glial cell ligand mediating selective neuronal growth and axon targeting (Sanz et al., 2017), and two of its neuronal receptors, netrin-G1 (Ntng1) and thy-1 membrane glycoprotein (Thy1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published ligand-receptor interaction data.

claim: About one-third of ligand-receptor pairs between glia and neurons showed strong age dependency.
source: We found 85 glial cell ligands of neuron receptors and 70 neuron ligands of glial cell receptors in our SCN proteome, and, more interestingly, about one-third of ligand-receptor pairs showed strong age dependency (Figure 4—source data 3 and 4), e.g., limbic system-associated membrane protein (Lsamp), a glial cell ligand mediating selective neuronal growth and axon targeting (Sanz et al., 2017), and two of its neuronal receptors, netrin-G1 (Ntng1) and thy-1 membrane glycoprotein (Thy1).
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: 21/90 known myelin proteins within the myelin proteome were differentially regulated by age.
source: In this respect, it is noteworthy that 21/90 known myelin proteins within the myelin proteome (Siems et al., 2020; Figure 2D) were differentially regulated by age, including highly abundant structural myelin proteins such as myelin basic protein (Mbp) and myelin protein P0 (Mpz) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Mbp and Mpz were significantly enriched in both male and female 14-week SCN.
source: In line with previous reports in mice and zebrafish (Siems et al., 2021), Mbp and Mpz were significantly enriched in both male and female 14-week SCN, reflecting myelin assembly and axonal development with age.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data and comparison with published literature.

claim: CD59A glycoprotein (Cd59a) was more abundant at adult age.
source: Similarly, CD59A glycoprotein (Cd59a), a sparsely expressed myelin protein associated with protection against complement-mediated lysis (Zeis et al., 2016), was more abundant at adult age (Figure 4D) as described previously in mouse brains (Siems et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4D and comparison with published literature.

claim: Some myelin DEPs appear to be specific for female (Bcas1, Ca2, Cadm4, Dynll1) or male (Itgb4) SCN in dependence on age.
source: Note, however, that some myelin DEPs appear to be specific for female (Bcas1, Ca2, Cadm4, Dynll1) or male (Itgb4) SCN in dependence on age – a fact that has not been investigated in previous studies, which mostly focused on male mice (Siems et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: 58 DEPs (in skin) and 33 DEPs (in SCN) were observed in a sex-dependent manner within the same age group.
source: In our proteome dataset, we observed 58 DEPs (in skin) and 33 DEPs (in SCN) in a sex-dependent manner within the same age group (Figure 5A and B, Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Sex-dependent changes were much less pronounced in 4-week compared to 14-week skin and SCN.
source: Of note, sex-dependent DEPs differed by age. For example, sex-dependent changes were much less pronounced in 4-week compared to 14-week skin (Figure 5A) and SCN (Figure 5B) in line with our initial PCA (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: No sex-dependent DEPs were observed at 4 weeks in SCN.
source: Interestingly, we did not observe any sex-dependent DEPs at 4 weeks in SCN (Figure 5B, orange circle).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 'Regulation of complement activation' was significantly enriched in both skin and SCN in sex comparisons at 14 weeks.
source: For example, 'regulation of complement activation' was significantly enriched in both skin and SCN in sex comparisons at 14 weeks (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Among 123 DEGs from a previous transcriptomics study on mouse hind paw skin, 42 proteins were quantified in the skin dataset, of which 14 were sexually dimorphic at 4 weeks and/or 14 weeks.
source: A previous transcriptomics study on mouse hind paw skin revealed 123 DEGs comparing female with male mice aged 8–12 weeks (Mecklenburg et al., 2020). Among these 123 DEGs, we quantified 42 proteins in our skin dataset, of which 14 were sexually dimorphic at 4 weeks and/or 14 weeks (Figure 5—source data 2; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) in line with published data (Mecklenburg et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published transcriptomics data.

claim: The proteome results harbor 329 out of 907 disease genes from human skin disease transcriptomic profiles.
source: Intriguingly, our proteome results harbor 329 out of 907 disease genes, of which 27 proteins showed significant age and/or sex dependency across varied skin diseases (Figure 6A, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with skin disease databases shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 27 proteins from skin disease-related genes showed significant age and/or sex dependency across varied skin diseases.
source: Intriguingly, our proteome results harbor 329 out of 907 disease genes, of which 27 proteins showed significant age and/or sex dependency across varied skin diseases (Figure 6A, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data and comparison with disease databases.

claim: Among 841 pain genes, 245 were quantified in the SCN proteome.
source: Among 841 pain genes, 245 were quantified in our SCN proteome (Figure 6D, Figure 6—source data 4 ).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with pain gene databases shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 132 of the pain-related proteins displayed significant changes (q-value ≤ 0.05) by age and/or sex.
source: Intriguingly, 132 of these pain-related proteins displayed significant changes (q-value ≤ 0.05) by age and/or sex (Figure 6—source data 4), of which examples are given in Figure 6F.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: Angiotensin I-converting enzyme (Ace) exhibits pronounced age and sex differences.
source: For instance, angiotensin I-converting enzyme (Ace) exhibits pronounced age and sex differences while its family member Ace2 only showed age differences (i.e., higher expression in adult mice).
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: Ace2 has been described to be associated with increased risk of nonspecific orofacial symptoms in the OPPERA prospective study.
source: Ace2 has been described to be associated with increased risk of nonspecific orofacial symptoms in the OPPERA (Smith et al., 2013) prospective study, and Ace is linked to migraine and potentially higher frequency as well as susceptibility (Dandona et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Smith et al., 2013 and Dandona et al., 2007.

claim: Ace is linked to migraine and potentially higher frequency as well as susceptibility.
source: Ace2 has been described to be associated with increased risk of nonspecific orofacial symptoms in the OPPERA (Smith et al., 2013) prospective study, and Ace is linked to migraine and potentially higher frequency as well as susceptibility (Dandona et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dandona et al., 2007.

claim: FK506 binding protein 51 (Fkbp5) displayed significant age and sex differences.
source: The FK506 binding protein 51 (Fkbp5) also displayed significant age and sex differences, with its expression being lower in female adults but higher in male adults compared to 4-week mice.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data.

claim: Fkbp5 polymorphisms predict persistent musculoskeletal pain after traumatic stress exposure.
source: Fkbp5 is a glucocorticoid receptor co-chaperone, and its polymorphisms predict persistent musculoskeletal pain after traumatic stress exposure (Bortsov et al., 2013; Linnstaedt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bortsov et al., 2013 and Linnstaedt et al., 2018.

claim: Fkbp5 is generally involved in the acute stress response linked to stress-related disorders in humans via the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.
source: Moreover, it is generally involved in the acute stress response linked to stress-related disorders in humans via the hypothalamic-pituitaryadrenal (HPA) axis (Häusl et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Häusl et al., 2021.

claim: Variations in serpin peptidase inhibitor clade A member 6 (Serpina6) are associated with the HPA stress axis impacting the susceptibility to musculoskeletal pain.
source: Interestingly, variations in serpin peptidase inhibitor clade A member 6 (Serpina6), another pain gene with pronounced age differences and sex-opposite expression, are also associated with the HPA stress axis impacting the susceptibility to musculoskeletal pain (Holliday et al., 2010), the risk of cardiovascular disease, as well as gene expression in peripheral tissues (Crawford et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Holliday et al., 2010 and Crawford et al., 2021.

claim: Several candidate proteins previously reported to be regulated upon SNI in adult males exhibited age-dependent abundance differences in males but not in females.
source: Indeed, several candidate proteins we previously reported (Barry et al., 2018) to be regulated upon SNI in adult males, for example, angiotensin-converting enzyme (Ace), apolipoprotein E (Apoe), complement C3 (C3), progranulin (Grn), epidermal growth factor receptor (Egfr), and voltage-dependent calcium channel subunit alpha-2/delta-1 (Cacna2d1), exhibited age-dependent abundance differences in males but not in females (Figure 6—source data 5) – a fact that has not been known before and might crucially affect SNI-induced pathology.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previous SNI study data.

claim: DIA-PASEF outperformed DDA-PASEF in terms of the number of protein IDs quantified, the coefficients of variation (CVs), and quantitative correlations between technical replicates.
source: As expected, DIA-PASEF outperformed DDA-PASEF in all parameters (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the comparison data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In SCN, more than twice as many proteins (~8400 IDs) were quantified compared to a previous study using DIA-MS (3141 IDs).
source: For instance, in SCN, we quantified more than twice as many proteins (~8400 IDs, Figure 2C) as in our previous study using DIA-MS (3141 IDs) (Barry et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previous study data.

claim: DIA-NN outperformed other DIA data processing software in terms of peptide and protein identifications.
source: For example, Arnaud Droit and colleagues systematically evaluated and compared DIA data processing software (Gotti et al., 2021) such as DIA-NN, DIA-Umpire, OpenSWATH, ScaffoldDIA, Skyline, and Spectronaut: DIA-NN outperformed others in terms of peptide and protein identifications.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gotti et al., 2021.

claim: The study analyzed 16 biological replicates of paw skin and SCN samples.
source: In this study, we analyzed 16 biological replicates of paw skin and SCN samples to compare the proteome between (1) two age groups, that is, 4-week-old adolescent mice and 14-week-old adult mice, and (2) males and females (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The study compared the proteome between 4-week-old adolescent mice and 14-week-old adult mice.
source: In this study, we analyzed 16 biological replicates of paw skin and SCN samples to compare the proteome between (1) two age groups, that is, 4-week-old adolescent mice and 14-week-old adult mice, and (2) males and females (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods.

claim: The study compared the proteome between males and females.
source: In this study, we analyzed 16 biological replicates of paw skin and SCN samples to compare the proteome between (1) two age groups, that is, 4-week-old adolescent mice and 14-week-old adult mice, and (2) males and females (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods.

claim: The SCN is affected by a wide variety of motor and sensory neuropathologies induced by inflammation, trauma, and demyelination.
source: The SCN is affected by a wide variety of motor and sensory neuropathologies induced by inflammation, trauma, and demyelination.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about SCN pathologies.

claim: The skin can be impaired by several inflammatory diseases like atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and lupus erythematodes.
source: Similarly, the skin, as our interface to the outer world, can be impaired by several inflammatory diseases like atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and lupus erythematodes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about skin diseases.

claim: Both the skin and SCN are involved in nociception and (chronic) pain.
source: In addition, both the skin and SCN are involved in nociception and (chronic) pain.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about pain mechanisms.

claim: Two samples (Skin_Ma4w-4 and SCN_Fe4w-1) were excluded from the analysis due to significantly lower protein content than corresponding biological replicates.
source: Two samples (Skin_Ma4w-4 and SCN_Fe4w-1) were excluded from the following analysis due to significantly lower protein content than corresponding biological replicates.
evidence: This is stated in the methods section.

claim: Only proteins quantified in ≥ 75% of replicates in each experimental group were submitted to differential expression analysis.
source: Only proteins quantified in ≥ 75% of replicates in each experimental group were submitted to differential expression analysis, resulting in 6983 protein IDs and 6827 protein IDs for paw skin and SCN proteomes, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the methods section.

claim: Proteins with the adjusted p-value ≤ 0.05 and the absolute log2 FC ≥ 0.585 were considered as DEPs in each contrast.
source: Proteins with the adjusted (Benjamini and Hochberg, for multiple testing) p-value ≤ 0.05 (hereafter referred to as the q-value) and the absolute log2 FC ≥ 0.585, that is, an absolute FC of 1.5, were considered as DEPs in each contrast.
evidence: This is stated in the methods section.
